When the interior +2^30 is added to `total` (=2^80), the lost 2^30 goes into `correction`; any subsequent small low values (~1) whose `lost` terms are then added to `correction` (≈2^30, ulp 128) are silently rounded away until the -2^30 arrives, so those rows' low values are permanently lost from the final sum, which is exactly what the adversarial ±2^30 interior pair is designed to expose. Only if the permutation happens to place the two 2^30 entries adjacently (≈20% chance) would the exact-sum contract be met."}
